title: Rational Design of TDP-43 Derived alpha-Helical Peptide Inhibitors: an In-Silico Strategy to Prevent TDP-43 Aggregation in Neurodegenerative Disorders.
authors: Salaikumaran, Muthu Raj; Gopal, Pallavi P
journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
one_liner_zh: 该研究用分子对接和MD设计TDP-43衍生肽抑制剂，虽涉及蛋白-DNA结合蛋白但聚焦蛋白自身聚集，非TF-DNA互作体系，方法可迁移性有限。
abstract: TDP-43, an essential RNA/DNA-binding protein, is central to the pathology of neurodegenerative diseases such as Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis and Frontotemporal Dementia. Pathological mislocalization and aggregation of TDP-43 disrupts RNA splicing, mRNA stability, and mRNA transport, thereby impairing neuronal function and survival. The formation of amyloid-like TDP-43 filaments is largely facilitated by the destabilization of an alpha-helical segment within the disordered C-terminal region. In this study, we hypothesized that preventing the destabilization of the alpha-helical domain could potentially halt the growth of these pathological filaments. To explore this, we utilized a range of in-silico techniques to design and evaluate peptide-based therapeutics. Various pathological TDP-43 amyloid-like filament crystal structures were selected for their potential to inhibit the binding of additional TDP-43 monomers to the growing filaments. Our computational approaches included biophysical and secondary structure property prediction, molecular docking, 3D structure prediction, and molecular dynamics simulations. Through these techniques, we were able to assess the structure, stability, and binding affinity of these peptides in relation to pathological TDP-43 filaments. The results of our in-silico analyses identified a selection of promising peptides, which displayed a stable alpha-helical structure, exhibited an increased number of intramolecular hydrogen bonds within the helical domain, and demonstrated high binding affinities for pathological TDP-43 amyloid-like filaments. Additionally, molecular dynamics simulations provided further support for the stability of these peptides, as they exhibited lower root mean square deviations in their helical propensity over 100ns. These findings establish alpha-helical propensity peptides as potential lead molecules for the development of novel therapeutics against TDP-43 aggregation. This structure-based computational approach for rational design of peptide inhibitors opens a new direction in the search for effective interventions for ALS, FTD, and other related neurodegenerative diseases. The peptides identified as the most promising candidates in this study are currently subject to further testing and validation through both in vitro and in vivo experiments.
abstract_zh: TDP-43，一种必需的RNA/DNA结合蛋白，在肌萎缩侧索硬化症和额颞叶痴呆等神经退行性疾病的病理过程中起核心作用。TDP-43的病理学错误定位和聚集破坏了RNA剪接、mRNA稳定性和mRNA运输，从而损害神经元功能和存活。淀粉样TDP-43纤维的形成主要得益于无序C末端区域内α-螺旋片段的不稳定化。在本研究中，我们假设阻止α-螺旋结构域的不稳定化可能潜在地阻止这些病理纤维的生长。为探索此假设，我们利用一系列计算机模拟技术设计和评估基于肽的治疗方法。我们选择了多种病理TDP-43淀粉样纤维晶体结构，以评估其抑制额外TDP-43单体结合到生长纤维上的潜力。我们的计算方法包括生物物理和二级结构性质预测、分子对接、三维结构预测和分子动力学模拟。通过这些技术，我们能够评估这些肽相对于病理TDP-43纤维的结构、稳定性和结合亲和力。我们的计算机模拟分析结果识别出一批有前景的肽，它们显示出稳定的α-螺旋结构，在螺旋结构域内表现出增加的分子内氢键数量，并对病理TDP-43淀粉样纤维显示出高结合亲和力。此外，分子动力学模拟进一步支持了这些肽的稳定性，因为它们在100ns内螺旋倾向性的均方根偏差较低。这些发现确立了具有α-螺旋倾向性的肽作为开发针对TDP-43聚集的新型治疗方法的潜在先导分子。这种基于结构的计算设计肽抑制剂的方法为寻找ALS、FTD及其他相关神经退行性疾病的有效干预措施开辟了新方向。本研究中识别为最有前景候选物的肽目前正在通过体外和体内实验进行进一步测试和验证。
